desc:
You start with power units of power and a score of 0. There is a bag of tokens, where tokens[i] is the value of the i-th token. Each token can be played at most once, in any order, in one of two ways:

  • Face up: if your power is at least tokens[i], you may spend tokens[i] power to gain 1 score.
  • Face down: if your score is at least 1, you may spend 1 score to gain tokens[i] power.

You do not have to play every token. Return the largest score you can have at any moment.

tokens = [100], power = 50              -> 0
tokens = [100, 200], power = 150        -> 1
tokens = [100, 200, 300, 400], power = 200 -> 2

In the last example: play 100 face up (power 100, score 1), play 400 face down (power 500, score 0), then play 200 and 300 face up (power 0, score 2).
hints: Face up converts power into score, face down converts score back into power. Which tokens do you want to spend power on, and which do you want to sell for power?
Spend power on the cheapest tokens, and when you need power, sell the most valuable remaining token. Sort the tokens.

Use two pointers on the sorted array. If the smallest token is affordable, play it face up; otherwise, if you have score, play the largest token face down; otherwise stop. Track the best score seen along the way.
editorial: Each point of score costs a token's value in power, so you want the cheapest tokens face up. A token played face down returns its value in power, so you want the most valuable tokens face down. Sorting puts both ends where they are needed.

Keep pointers lo and hi on the sorted array. While lo ≤ hi: if power ≥ tokens[lo], play it face up (power decreases, score increases) and update the best score; else if the score is positive, play tokens[hi] face down and move hi left; else stop. Selling a token only makes sense when you cannot afford the cheapest one, which is why the best score is recorded after every face-up move and not only at the end.
Each token is touched once after the sort, so the time is O(n log n).
